subChunks.title: Accessibility Audit
subChunks.hookHtml: An accessibility audit is not a checkbox. It is a systematic examination of every interactive element, every piece of content, and every state in your application — against WCAG 2.2 criteria, keyboard navigation, screen reader behaviour, and motion sensitivity. This lesson provides the methodology and the Tailwind patterns that address each failure category.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "Accessibility is not a feature you add at the end. It is an architectural constraint you apply throughout. When a senior developer says 'we can make it accessible later,' the cost of that debt has already compounded. A Lead engineer prevents the debt from accruing."

The audit methodology

  1. Automated scan: run axe-core, Lighthouse, WAVE — catches ~30% of issues
  2. Keyboard navigation: tab through every interactive element, verify focus indicators
  3. Screen reader testing: NVDA/JAWS on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS/iOS
  4. Zoom to 200%: verify layout doesn't break at 2x browser zoom
  5. Colour contrast check: verify 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI components
  6. Motion review: check every animation for prefers-reduced-motion pair

Focus indicator audit — the most common failure

/* ❌ Invisible focus indicator */
button { outline: none; }  /* or: @apply outline-none */

/* ❌ Low-contrast focus ring — passes automated but fails visual review */
.btn { @apply focus:ring-2 focus:ring-gray-200; }
/* gray-200 on white background: 1.2:1 contrast — fails */

/* ✅ WCAG-compliant focus indicator */
.btn { @apply focus:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2
              focus-visible:ring-indigo-600 focus-visible:ring-offset-2; }
/* indigo-600 on white: 4.7:1 — passes AA */

/* The ring-offset-2 is critical: creates a 2px white gap between
   the element and the ring, making the ring visible even when the
   element has a dark background */

Semantic HTML + ARIA audit

/* ❌ div-soup — no semantic information for screen readers */
<div class="nav">
  <div onClick={handleNav} class="nav-item">Home</div>
</div>

/* ✅ Semantic HTML — roles conveyed to screen readers */
<nav aria-label="Main navigation">
  <a href="/" class="...">Home</a>
</nav>

/* ❌ Icon button with no accessible name */
<button class="p-2">
  <svg ...></svg>
</button>

/* ✅ Icon button with sr-only label */
<button class="p-2" aria-label="Close dialog">
  <svg aria-hidden="true" ...></svg>
  <span class="sr-only">Close dialog</span>
</button>

Colour contrast — the systematic check

/* Tools: */
/* - WebAIM Contrast Checker (manual) */
/* - axe DevTools (automated) */
/* - Figma Contrast Plugin (design phase) */

/* Common Tailwind failure patterns: */
text-gray-400 on white:     3.5:1 — fails AA for normal text
text-gray-500 on white:     4.6:1 — passes AA
text-gray-400 on gray-50:   3.3:1 — fails
text-indigo-300 on white:   2.5:1 — fails (use indigo-700+)

/* Semantic token solution: */
@theme {
  --color-muted-foreground: oklch(0.50 0.01 270);  /* ≥4.5:1 on white */
  --color-placeholder: oklch(0.60 0.01 270);        /* ≥3:1 — large text only */
}

Motion sensitivity audit

/* Every animation must have a reduced-motion pair */

/* ❌ Animation without reduced-motion */
.card { @apply animate-fade-in; }

/* ✅ Paired with motion-reduce: */
.card { @apply animate-fade-in motion-reduce:animate-none; }

/* ❌ Continuous animation */
.spinner { @apply animate-spin; }

/* ✅ Respect preference */
.spinner { @apply animate-spin motion-reduce:animate-[spin_1.5s_linear_infinite]; }
/* At reduced motion: spin continues but slower — still communicates loading */
/* OR: motion-reduce:hidden + show static indicator */

Running the automated audit

# axe-cli for command-line auditing
npm install -g @axe-core/cli
axe http://localhost:3000 --save report.json

# Playwright + axe for CI
import { checkA11y } from 'axe-playwright';
test('homepage has no a11y violations', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await checkA11y(page, null, {
    runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'] }
  });
});

# jest-axe for unit tests
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);
test('Button has no a11y violations', async () => {
  const { container } = render(<Button>Click me</Button>);
  expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations();
});

Solomon: "WCAG 2.2 AA is the legal standard in the EU (EN 301 549), the UK (PSBAR), and increasingly in the US (ADA digital guidance). A Lead engineer understands the legal context. This is not optional compliance — it is risk management."

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: Run axe. Tab through every interactive element. Test with a screen reader. Check every colour pair. Pair every animation with motion-reduce:. This is the audit. It is not glamorous work. It is necessary work. A Lead engineer does it before shipping, not after receiving a complaint.

storyBeats.speaker: Compliant focus indicator pattern

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build an accessibility audit checklist UI showing common failure patterns and their fixes:

  • .audit-page: max-w-2xl, mx-auto, p-6, space-y-3
  • .audit-item: bg-white, rounded-xl, border, p-4, flex, items-start, gap-3
  • .audit-item--pass: border-emerald-200
  • .audit-item--fail: border-red-200
  • .audit-icon: w-5, h-5, flex-none, mt-0.5
  • .audit-icon--pass: text-emerald-500
  • .audit-icon--fail: text-red-500
  • .audit-content: flex-1
  • .audit-title: text-sm, font-semibold, text-gray-900
  • .audit-desc: text-sm, text-gray-600, mt-0.5
  • .audit-code: mt-2, text-xs, font-mono, bg-gray-50, rounded, px-2, py-1, text-gray-700
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
✓

Focus indicator visible

focus-visible:ring-2 with ring-offset-2 passes WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7

focus:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-indigo-600 focus-visible:ring-offset-2
✗

Focus indicator missing

outline-none without a focus-visible replacement removes the focus ring entirely

focus:outline-none ← v3 semantic changed in v4
✓

Colour contrast passes AA

text-gray-700 on white: 7.4:1 — passes both AA and AAA

text-gray-700 → 7.4:1 on white
✗

Animation not reduced

animate-pulse without motion-reduce: pair may trigger vestibular issues

animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Design a complete accessibility audit report from scratch for a hypothetical button component. Include sections for: focus indicator status, ARIA attributes, colour contrast ratios (show actual numbers), keyboard interaction, motion sensitivity, and screen reader announcement. Mark each as pass/fail with the specific WCAG criterion. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Walk through a systematic accessibility audit of a navigation bar component: what automated tools you would run, what you would check manually with a keyboard, what you would listen for with a screen reader, and what motion-related checks you would perform. For each failure you find, explain the WCAG criterion it violates and the Tailwind fix.

questions.prompt: What WCAG 2.2 success criterion governs focus indicators, and what is the minimum requirement at Level AA?
options: SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible — any keyboard-operable UI component must have a visible focus indicator when it receives keyboard focus
SC 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum — the focus indicator must have a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background
SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — focus indicators must have programmatic labels
SC 2.1.1 Keyboard — focus must be visible to ensure keyboard navigability
questions.answer: SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible — any keyboard-operable UI component must have a visible focus indicator when it receives keyboard focus
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA) requires that any UI component that can be operated by keyboard shows a visible focus indicator when focused. WCAG 2.4.11 (2.2, Level AA) additionally specifies minimum focus indicator size and contrast. The Tailwind pattern focus:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-indigo-600 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 satisfies both criteria when the ring colour has sufficient contrast.

questions.prompt: An automated axe scan shows 0 violations, but a manual keyboard test shows the focused button has no visible ring. Why might this happen?
options: The button uses focus:outline-none without focus-visible:ring-2 — axe tests with all elements artificially focused, but doesn't reproduce keyboard-only focus styling which uses :focus-visible, not :focus
axe tests the DOM structure but doesn't evaluate CSS — it would not detect any styling issues
The ring is present but uses a colour with insufficient contrast — axe would report this as a colour contrast violation
axe catches 100% of focus indicator issues — if it passes, the focus ring must be present
questions.answer: The button uses focus:outline-none without focus-visible:ring-2 — axe tests with all elements artificially focused, but doesn't reproduce keyboard-only focus styling which uses :focus-visible, not :focus
questions.explanation: axe programmatically focuses elements to test focus indicators, but it applies :focus styles — not :focus-visible. In modern browsers, focus:ring-2 applies the ring when programmatically focused (which axe triggers), but focus-visible:ring-2 only applies when the element is focused via keyboard. If the button uses focus-visible: for the ring, axe may not catch its absence because axe's programmatic focusing triggers :focus, not :focus-visible. Always supplement automated scans with manual keyboard testing.

questions.prompt: A loading spinner uses animate-spin on an SVG icon. A user with vestibular disorder reports that continuous rotation triggers vertigo. What is the correct accessibility fix?
options: Add motion-reduce:animate-none and replace the spinner with a static 'Loading...' text or opacity-pulsing indicator for reduced-motion users
Remove the spinner and use a progress bar instead — spinners are always inaccessible
Add aria-hidden='true' to the spinner — hiding it from screen readers fixes the issue
Use a shorter animation duration: animate-[spin_0.5s_linear_infinite] — faster spin is less noticeable
questions.answer: Add motion-reduce:animate-none and replace the spinner with a static 'Loading...' text or opacity-pulsing indicator for reduced-motion users
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA) and the prefers-reduced-motion media feature address vestibular sensitivity. The fix is to respect the user's motion preference: motion-reduce:animate-none stops the rotation. But stopping the animation without an alternative removes the loading feedback — replace it with a static indicator or a very subtle opacity pulse (which doesn't involve spatial movement). Never increase animation speed as an accessibility measure.
